intro: Searching for a cyber insurance broker near you usually means you want someone local who can sit down with you, or at least talk through your situation properly, and explain what cyber cover actually involves. You may be running a small business, holding client data, or simply worried about ransomware and breaches after hearing about them in the news. A broker can compare insurers, spell out exclusions and stand beside you if you need to claim.
need_heading: What people searching for a cyber insurance broker usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a cyber insurance broker near them want clarity on what cover they actually need and someone accountable when things go wrong.
needs: You run a small business that holds customer or client data and want to know what happens if that data is breached.
You have been asked for cyber cover by a client, a supplier or a contract and need to understand what is being requested.
You are worried about ransomware locking your systems and want to know whether incident response support is included.
You want someone to compare insurers for you rather than working through policy wording alone.
You have a policy already but are unsure whether it covers social engineering or business interruption after an attack.
context_heading: What to understand before you choose a cyber insurance broker
context: Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm, so you can check them on the FCA register. Many brokers belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association (BIBA), and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute. A broker must understand your demands and needs, explain key policy features and exclusions, and tell you how they are paid.

Insurers will expect you to have basic security controls in place before they will offer cyber cover, so be ready to describe what you already do. It is also worth checking whether a policy includes incident response support and whether social engineering cover is part of it, as these are often the areas people overlook until they need them. If a complaint is not resolved, it can go to the Financial Ombudsman Service.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe what your business does and the kind of data you hold, as this shapes the cover you need.
Say roughly how many people work with you, so the broker understands the scale of your operation.
Explain whether a client, supplier or contract has asked you for cyber cover, and what they have specified.
Mention any security measures you already have in place, such as backups, multi-factor authentication or staff training.
Say whether you already hold a cyber policy and what you are unsure about in it.
Note whether you would prefer a broker you can meet locally or are happy to deal with one by phone or email.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the cyber insurance broker
questions: Are you authorised by the FCA, and can you tell me how you are paid for arranging this cover?
Does the policy include incident response support, and who would I call if I had a breach?
Is social engineering cover included, and what are the limits and exclusions?
What basic security controls will the insurer expect me to have in place?
How would business interruption after a cyber attack be handled under this policy?
What is excluded from the cover, and how would a claim actually work in practice?

faqs.q: Do I need cyber insurance if I already have business insurance?
faqs.a: Cyber cover is often separate from a standard business policy, and the two may not overlap in the way you expect. A broker can explain what your existing policy does and does not include so you can judge whether additional cover is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Will the insurer expect me to have security measures in place?
faqs.a: Insurers generally expect basic security controls before they will offer cyber cover. A broker can tell you what is typically looked for and how to describe what you already do.

faqs.q: What is social engineering cover and do I need it?
faqs.a: Social engineering cover relates to losses where someone is tricked into transferring money or giving away information. It is worth asking whether it is included, as it is often an area people overlook until they need it.

faqs.q: How do I check that a broker is properly authorised?
faqs.a: Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm. You can check them on the FCA register, and many brokers also belong to BIBA or hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute.

extra_heading: Meeting a local cyber insurance broker for the first time
extra: Searching for a cyber insurance broker near you often means you would rather deal with someone face to face, or at least by phone, than work through an online form alone. A local broker can talk through your setup in plain terms, ask what you store and where, and explain what a policy would and would not cover. That conversation usually tells you quickly whether they understand businesses like yours.

At a first meeting, expect to be asked how your business handles customer information, whether you use cloud services, and what you would do if your systems were locked by ransomware. The broker will use this to approach insurers and to explain exclusions, limits and how a claim would actually run. Come with your existing policy if you have one, and be ready to describe any basic security controls you already have in place.

It is worth asking early whether the broker deals with cyber cover regularly, and how they are paid, as they must tell you this. If you want to compare more than one option, you can speak to several brokers before deciding, as each will quote you directly. A good first meeting leaves you clearer on what you are buying, not just on the price.

extra_faqs.q: Is it better to use a broker near me than one further away?
extra_faqs.a: For cyber cover, much can be handled by phone or email, so distance matters less than whether the broker understands your type of business. A local broker may suit you if you prefer meeting in person to talk through sensitive details about your systems and data. Either way, check they are authorised by the FCA before you proceed.

extra_faqs.q: What should I bring to a first meeting with a cyber insurance broker?
extra_faqs.a: Bring details of what your business does, the data you hold, and any security measures already in place, such as backups or staff training. If you have an existing policy, bring it so the broker can see what is already covered. It also helps to know what a client or contract has asked you for, if that is what prompted your search.
